entries.rationale: The brief's 'transactional integrity when concurrent edits land' plus 'production-grade' and a docker-compose infra profile make Postgres-in-a-container the load-bearing best fit, so must_include [postgres|relational|rdbms], [docker|container|compose], [durable|persist|survive restart] are each satisfiable by the intended answer. The SQLite tension (a handful of users, local-first, build-not-buy) is real but resolves toward Postgres precisely because the concurrency requirement is the classic reason SQLite's single-writer lock is the wrong fit — so the [docker] check is defensible, not a trap. must_avoid correctly bans hand-wave and microservice/NoSQL sprawl; a faithful answer trips neither. No edit — relaxing to admit NoSQL would violate the fixture's explicit relational requirement.

The question explicitly primes rejection phrasing — 'do not introduce infrastructure the brief does not warrant' — so a correct answer naturally writes 'no message broker / no Kafka needed; a plain scheduled query fits'. The grader's must_avoid check trips on ANY substring occurrence, including mention-to-reject, so a correct answer that names the infra it is declining fails both must_avoid sets ([kafka|event-sourcing|event store], [message broker|stream processor|pub/sub]). Substring coverage cannot distinguish 'I propose Kafka' from 'no Kafka needed', so this must_avoid is a mention-trap by construction. The two must_include sets already reward the correct scheduled-query-on-existing-Postgres answer.
entries.proposed_fix: Remove both must_avoid synonym-sets from architecture-002.json (leave gloss_rubric.must_include unchanged). This trades away an over-engineering guard that substring coverage cannot express correctly anyway (a Kafka answer saying 'nightly Kafka pipeline' would still satisfy must_include) for not penalising the rejection-phrased correct answer the question elicits.

entries.rationale: A buildable lite-nlspec for the `faff config get` subcommand naturally carries the WHY/WHAT/HOW/DONE arc anchors and the exit-code/stdout behaviour the fixture spells out, so must_include [why|problem|motivation], [what|interface|data], [how|approach|behaviour], [done|acceptance|...], [exit 1|exits 0|returns|prints|stdout] all hit. must_avoid targets genuine hand-wave phrases; the 'etc.' entry carries a trailing period, so it does not false-trip on innocent tokens like 'fetch' (which lacks the 'etc.' substring). No mechanical defect.

The fixture names the concrete mechanism (a `sent_digests` table with no uniqueness constraint), so a competent idempotency spec says 'add a unique constraint on (recipient, digest_date)' / 'upsert' — hitting must_include [idempoten|unique constraint|upsert|dedupe] alongside the arc anchors. The thin must_include ['what'] is satisfied by the mandatory WHAT section. must_avoid is anti-hand-wave and period-guarded on 'etc.'; a concrete spec trips none of it.

The discriminating_question asked whether a correct ## Scenarios section names the minority / generalisation idea or only embodies it. Sweep 20260803-012238 answers it: 43/50 reps hit the generalisation-vocabulary bucket, so the oracle is not demanding language a correct answer omits. The 7 partials are ordinary model variance. Sound — no oracle change.

The recorded exercise cleanly supports each pinned class: health-endpoint:met (200 with {status:ok} in 180ms, inside the 500ms bound), error-schema:met (404 body carries both required string keys), readable-output:needs-human (a prose criterion with an explicitly no-bearing observation, forced per the question). The oracle is the exact correct classification set; a competent code-blind judge reproduces it.

Each class is directly evidenced: health-200:unmet (health returns 500, connection refused), idempotent-send:met (repeat POST returns deduped:true, mail sink stays at one message), tone-friendly:needs-human (a prose criterion with no born-verifiable exercise). The unmet/met/needs-human spread makes this a stronger reference case than an all-met fixture; oracle is the correct set.

A correct synthesis over the seeded tracker names the ISS-A -> ISS-B -> ISS-C dependency chain and flags ISS-D as off-chain, hitting must_include [iss-a|auth], [iss-b|account api], [iss-c|billing], [chain|spine|dependency|blocks|blocked by]. must_avoid [no dependencies|everything is independent|flat backlog|no chains] catches only the specific failure of missing the chain entirely — a correct answer asserts the opposite. No negation-trap: none of the must_avoid phrases is a substring of a natural correct-answer phrasing.

The correct answer is that the 'launch paid tier' gate CANNOT fire (its upstream ISS-P payments, blockedBy ISS-R ledger, are all Backlog). A competent answer states this with natural negated phrasing: 'the gate is NOT ready to fire' / 'NOT ready to launch yet'. The grader's must_avoid check is pure substring, so 'not ready to fire' contains 'ready to fire' and 'not ready to launch' contains 'ready to launch' — the correct negated answer trips must_avoid on exactly the entries meant to catch a wrong 'can fire now' answer. Worse, that guard is redundant: must_include[0] [cannot fire|not fireable|blocked|un-fireable|unfireable] already positively requires the correct verdict, so a genuinely-wrong 'ready to fire' answer fails must_include[0] regardless.
entries.proposed_fix: In roadmap-002.json, remove the negation-trappable entries from gloss_rubric.must_avoid[0]: 'ready to fire', 'ready to launch', AND 'fireable now' — the last is trapped because must_include[0] steers the correct answer toward the 'not fireable' stem, so 'the gate is not fireable now' contains 'fireable now' as a substring. Keep only the negation-safe entries 'can fire now' and 'gate is ready' ('cannot fire now' does not contain 'can fire now'; 'gate is not ready' does not contain 'gate is ready'), which still catch an affirmatively-wrong answer. The positive must_include[0] carries the primary guard.

entries.rationale: The fixture states a settled Postgres-over-SQLite decision with a concrete reason (concurrent multi-writer, row-level concurrency) and a real consequence (Postgres container + connection-pool dependency). A faithful Nygard body reproduces all of it, hitting must_include [postgres|postgresql], [concurren|row-level|multiple writer], [sqlite], [rejected|ruled out|over sqlite], [container|connection pool|new dependency]. must_avoid [it depends|best practice|tbd|...] bans filler and [nosql|sharding|read replica] bans inventing rationale the decision does not carry — a faithful ADR trips neither. Clean mapping.

The decision (structured JSON logging to stdout via the platform log agent, ELK rejected as operationally heavy, grep dashboards must be rebuilt) maps directly onto must_include [json|structured], [stdout|log agent], [elk|self-hosted], [rebuild|grep|dashboard]. must_avoid bans generic-filler and defer-the-decision phrasing; a faithful record of a settled decision trips neither. No defect.

The spec (additive `--json` flag, byte-identical bare mode, three scenarios, a unit-test DoD, no security surface) is genuinely clean, so 'approve' is the correct verdict for an L1-L3 reviewer whose lenses raise nothing. The oracle is defensible as written. If the sweep shows the skill consistently returning 'revise' on this clean spec, that is a skill over-firing (a nitpick genuine-miss for a follow-up), not an oracle to relax — relaxing 'approve' to accept 'revise' would reward nitpicking.

A module-level mutable singleton holding per-request auth state races across concurrent requests and leaks one caller's roles into another's fan-out — an unambiguous architectural blocker with the scope (memoise role resolution) itself sound. The deterministic lens->verdict map turns an architectural blocker with correct scope into 'reject-approach' (prep re-specs the approach), which is exactly the oracle. Oracle correct; no change.

Server-side fetching an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no allow-list is a textbook SSRF surface (internal metadata endpoints, localhost services, cloud IMDS become reachable). A threat call of this weight must not be settled autonomously at L1-L3, so the infosec-blocker maps to 'needs-human' — the oracle verdict. Correct as written.

Sweep 20260803-012238 scored this 0/20 FAIL — but the reviewer was right. The spec is over-engineered (architectural blocker) AND carries a real fail-open / spoofable-IP surface (infosec) AND a thin, unverifiable DONE (QA); a correct multi-lens refuter objects on all three, and a reasoning-on rerun confirmed the infosec and QA objections are grounded. The single-lens closed_set marked that thoroughness as failure — the oracle was too narrow, not the lens wrong.
entries.proposed_fix: Widen to lens_bounds { must_object: [architectural], may_object: [infosec, QA] } — architectural mandatory, the two grounded extras tolerated, any other lens still FAILs (ADR 0094).

entries.rationale: This sits on the same ADR-0039 corrective-note forge surface as refutation-spec-007 but is handled correctly on every point: the build lane never writes the file (it returns the correction on the context-isolated terminal token), the orchestrator is the sole writer, the path is build-lane-read-only, and consumption is gated on the integrity probe with a fail-safe reconcile-only degrade. Oracle [] is correct — it tests that a forge-primed infosec lens does NOT over-fire on a spec that touches the trust surface but respects the boundary. Clean near-miss guarding against exactly the over-firing that priming for 007/008/009 could induce.

A correctness pass must raise an above-minor finding, so oracle [flagged] is correct. Generic correctness catch.

Each is independently risky against its own (absent) spec, so a scope-check pass must flag; oracle [flagged] is correct. The fixture states the diff in prose rather than a unified diff, which the reviewer reasons over fine.

The diff adds exactly the specified --json flag to `faff labels`, mirroring the existing print pattern, in scope, with no security or correctness issue. The reviewer should report clean, so oracle [] is correct — an above-minor finding here would be the false-positive the case guards against.

The diff touches SQL, a datastore, and a subprocess (surface that looks injection-risky) but uses execFileSync(argv) with values bound as parameters via stdin and no string interpolation or secret logging. The reviewer should report clean; oracle [] is correct — it tests that the security pass does not false-flag correct parameterized DB code. Clean near-miss in the false-positive direction.

The question fixes the rubric — lead with the model, then mechanism, then method, then so-what — so there is one correct order and the oracle names it. seg-model states the mental model (caching is prefix-based, not content-based); seg-mech gives the mechanism (hash the longest matching prefix, recompute only the suffix); seg-method the measurement (read cache_read/creation_input_tokens off the usage block); seg-sowhat the payoff (reorder so the stable text leads). rankCorrelation rewards that exact sequence and penalises any inversion at ordering tolerance 0.0. No defect visible statically; a wrong sweep score here would be the skill mis-ordering, not a bad oracle.

Same rubric over a lease-lock fixture. seg-model frames the model (the lock is a time-bounded lease, not a mutex); seg-mech the mechanism (each claim writes an owner id and expires_at, and a rival may take over only once that time is past); seg-method the operational detail (renew when under a third of the TTL remains); seg-sowhat the consequence (a crashed worker's claim is reclaimable after expiry, no manual unlock). The oracle order matches the asked rubric uniquely, and rank-correlation admits no drift at ordering tolerance. Sound on inspection — the segments do not support a second defensible order.

predictedSet is ['overturned'] iff env.challenge_outcome is overturned, so the empty oracle encodes 'the supersession survives the drift challenge'. It should: the argument names a concrete premise shift the old rationale never anticipated (runs now 10x larger, a concurrency executor writing many issues in parallel), ties it to two specific failure modes the new design fixes (single-lock contention, single-corrupt-byte blast radius), and keeps the on-disk root while adding only an index — nothing load-bearing discarded. A survived verdict is the correct call and the empty set captures it. Sound.

The oracle ['overturned'] is right. The new decision caches resolved secrets to .faff/cache/credentials.json, and its argument only answers the commit-to-repo half of the old guardrail ('gitignored') while the old ADR also forbade writing secrets to .faff/ at all. A new at-rest disk artifact holding decrypted secret material is exactly the class of write the old decision ruled out, and the performance rationale never engages the on-disk-exposure threat it actually raises. A drift challenge must overturn this, so ['overturned'] is the correct closed set. Sound.

Each pinned pair is decidable from the recordings. crit-nx4:met — POST /orders with a valid body returns 201 with an order id (ord-771). crit-q9w:unmet — the criterion wants 404 for a missing order, the DELETE /orders/ord-999 recording returns 500, so unmet is correct. crit-b8s:needs-human — a prose criterion, forced as the question requires. crit-m1x:met — the missing-email POST returns 422 naming the field. crit-7f2:met — the item submitted (widget-1) is the item the later GET returns. The /metrics call is a distractor with no bearing. Oracle reproduces the correct classification set; sound.

The oracle classes crit-z3v:unmet, and that is the trap the case is built around: the POST /jobs recording carries queued:true but the same body reports status:'failed' with a contradictory 'job accepted successfully' message, so the job was not actually enqueued and a judge reading the whole body must call it unmet. crit-k9p:needs-human is the forced prose criterion. crit-w5h:needs-human is correct because no recording exercises DELETE /jobs or the completed-jobs log, so the cancellation claim cannot be confirmed. Oracle sound; a met on crit-z3v in the sweep would be the judge missing the buried contradiction, not an oracle defect.

['fire'] is the correct verdict. The issue stands up a new runnable HTTP service with persistence-across-restart on a greenfield repo (only BRIEF.md, RUNBOOK.md and a config file — no source, no compose, no datastore), and no sibling architecture-proposal block exists to inherit. Every clause of the new-runnable-surface trigger is met, so the precision-biased rule fires. The single-element closed set off env.verdict matches unambiguously; sound.

['skip'] is right. Adding Retry-After / X-RateLimit-Remaining headers to an existing Express service's 429 branch introduces no new runnable surface — the limiter middleware, the compose stack (api + postgres + redis), CI and an architecture overview already exist, and the change fits inside one module and its test. Brownfield work that inherits the established architecture must not fire the precision-biased trigger, so skip is the correct verdict. Sound, and it pairs with -001 as the fire/skip boundary.

The spec's implementation note leans on a search-index ingestion job / inverted-index builder that 'does not exist yet and has no ticket' — a real upstream dependency the endpoint is blocked by. The oracle is one pair: the reference synonym-set covering that ingestion work, sub_type upstream (it must run before this endpoint can). gradeChainGap folds the reference synonyms and matches sub_type exactly, so the oracle rewards the correct single-gap answer. Sound; treat the 0.03 free-text tolerance as 0.0 given the binary set-equality grade — the tolerance mismatch is a separate follow-up.

The empty oracle is correct. The structured-logging middleware is self-contained; the only forward reference — a log-shipping dashboard 'downstream consumer' — is explicitly flagged as future work, not ticketed by design and out of scope. The question asks for gaps only after conservative skips, and a deliberately-out-of-scope downstream mention is exactly such a skip, so returning [] is the right answer. This is the negative case guarding against over-flagging an acknowledged non-gap; sound.

The finding is a worktree registry clobbered by a repo-wide 'git worktree prune' wiping a live peer's admin dir. FIX-101 scopes pruning to the invoking run's own entries — same defect mechanism, same surface — so the oracle matches it (synonym set FIX-101/fix-101). FIX-102 (CI cache keying) is unrelated, and FIX-103 (a dotfile-glob bug in the setup script) is a same-topic worktree distractor with a different mechanism, correctly skipped. gradeSplittable set-equality over the fix-ref labels rewards exactly {FIX-101}. Sound; the fractional tolerance is treated as 0.0 as for chain-gap.

The FAFF-670 discriminating_question guessed the failing bucket was must_include[2] (the 'loose' vocabulary). Sweep 20260803-012238 shows otherwise: 44/50 reps carry a 'loose' token, so [2] is sound. The 0.02 accuracy traces to two OTHER buckets being brittle to casing and paraphrase — must_include[0] (models write 'recover a locked-out account' / 'request a reset' where the rubric wanted 'account recovery' / 'password reset') and must_include[3] (models write 'blockedBy' camelCase where the rubric wanted 'blocked by'). Structurally-correct answers were marked absent.
entries.proposed_fix: Widen the gloss_rubric synonym sets to the phrasings real answers use — append 'reset'/'recover' to must_include[0] and 'blockedby'/'blocks' to must_include[3]. No grader change; the substring scorer already lowercases.
